Dāva, ‘forest fire,’ is mentioned in the Atharvaveda and the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa. In the latter work such fires are referred to as occurring in spring. According to Sieg, a hymn of the Rigveda describes a forest fire. Watchers were employed to guard against surprise from such conflagrations (dāva-pa).
Foot notes vii. 45, 2.
xi. 2, 7, 32.
Die Sagenstoffe des ṛgveda, 44 et seq.
x. 142. Sieg's interpretation of this hymn is not at all probable.
Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xxx. 16; taittirīya brāhmaṇa, iii. 4, 11, 1.

Dāva-su Āṅgirasa, a seer of Sāmans, or chants, is mentioned in the pañcaviṃśa brāhmaṇa.
Foot notes xxv. 5, 12, 14. Cf. Hillebrandt, Vedische Mythologie, 2, 160.
